articles.title: Islam can NOT be Undisputed Champion…
articles.description: The UFC has announced Carlos Prates vs. Michael Morales for an interim championship while Islam Makhachev remains the undisputed champion—and I have a problem with the terminology. By definition, how can an interim champion exist alongside an undisputed champion? We saw a version of this before with Tom Aspinall and Jon Jones, but Islam’s situation raises a different question. Islam isn’t out because of an injury or illness. If Prates or Morales becomes interim champion, doesn’t that mean Islam’s championship is now disputed? I wouldn’t necessarily have handled the situation differently. But the question remains: Is Islam Makhachev still the undisputed champion? articles.title: Volkanovski vs. Gaethje Is a TERRIBLE Idea
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski has a habit of making his career harder than it needs to be. Instead of chasing the easiest matchup and biggest payday, Volk consistently looks for the guy who has earned the opportunity. But this time, he may have gotten something exactly right. Volkanovski wants to beat Movsar Evloev and then move to 155 for a retirement fight against Justin Gaethje. I initially thought the idea had virtually no chance of happening. Then Volk's camp offered an alternative: if he doesn't get Gaethje, he'll stay at featherweight and defend against Aljamain Sterling. Those are two very different nights of business for the UFC. Whether Volk intended it as leverage or not, he may have just played his strongest card. #UFC #MMA #AlexanderVolkanovski #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Does ONE Liver Shot Win a Round?
articles.description: Petr Yan landed the best shot of the third round against Merab Dvalishvili, a body shot that clearly hurt him. But was that one shot enough to win the entire round? That’s what I’m trying to understand. Take that body shot away, and I think Merab clearly won the round on pressure, output, takedowns, and control. All three judges gave the round to Yan. The rules prioritize damage, but what exactly qualifies as damage? Is visibly hurting your opponent enough? Does damage have to leave something we can actually see? I’m not claiming the judges got it wrong. I’m asking how we’re supposed to apply the standard consistently. I had Merab winning three rounds to two. #UFC #MMA #MerabDvalishvili #PetrYan #ChaelSonnen

articles.title: Alexander Volkov Deserves Our Support
articles.description: Alexander Volkov has the wins, the record, and the ranking. What I’ve been waiting for is for him to actually make some noise and advocate for himself. He finally did it. articles.title: Alexander Volkanovski: UFC 333 Post-Fight Press Conference | SICK and Still Finished Evloev
articles.description: Alexander Volkanovski’s full UFC 333 post-fight press conference after his second-round finish of previously unbeaten Movsar Evloev in Abu Dhabi. articles.title: Josh Hokit is one win away from becoming the biggest star in MMA
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is not ready to let the Bruce Buffer and Josh Hokit thing go, and he wants to be clear about why: this is not against Bruce, who he calls awesome and a friend. He is discussing the topic Bruce brought up, the idea that the way Hokit speaks is somehow the problem. Chael's case starts with the stakes. Josh Hokit is one win away from being the biggest star in MMA, and that win would make him the first undefeated, undisputed heavyweight champion the sport has ever had. Then comes the question that proves the point: could Hokit outdraw Sean O'Malley, Alex Pereira, Ilia Topuria or Justin Gaethje right now? Nobody is sure, and the fact that nobody is sure is the answer. Those men are world champions and former champions. Hokit is neither. He is the undefeated number one contender about to sell out Madison Square Garden, and he is already in that conversation. From there Chael turns Bruce's comment inside out with the laws of logic. If the way Josh speaks is wrong, the opposite has to be right, and the opposite is dead silence: no press conferences, no interviews, no need for Joe Rogan at all. Or he could speak like everybody else, and Chael performs that version too, the safe answer that thanks everybody and says nothing. Nobody wants either version. When you speak to Hokit you get the different sides of him instead, and when he is about to talk, people in living rooms and bars go quiet to hear him. Chael says he has only witnessed that twice before, with Rampage Jackson and then Conor McGregor. The UFC follows a code, the same code that never shut Sean Strickland out of a single media opportunity, and Chael says that code will be extended to Hokit. Subscribe for more from Chael Sonnen and tell us in the comments: should Hokit change how he talks, or is that exactly why everybody stops to listen? articles.title: Floyd vs Conor 2, Who Writes the Check?
articles.description: Floyd Mayweather is talking about Conor McGregor again, and Chael Sonnen says the whole situation feels very different this time. Chael shares what Conor told him personally when he asked him about Floyd during a fight week: anytime Conor thinks of Floyd, he just sees dollar signs. From there, Chael breaks down how Pretty Boy Floyd was not a star before 2005, how the Money Mayweather gimmick, the watches, the cash, and the rap-video presentation, is what actually made people care, and why that same gimmick lands very differently when you are publicly calling for a fight because you need the money. He also questions the money stories the pundits repeated for years, including the Forbes highest-paid-athlete claims, and asks a simple question nobody in the room could answer on one of the biggest podcasts in the world: if Floyd was paid $100 million to fight Conor, who wrote the check? Then Chael turns to Floyd himself. Boxing only exists because somebody is willing to lose a lot of money to be tied to the tough guy business, and the man who wrote that check took his beating and got out. The Money Team, presented alongside Showtime Sports as a real promotion, is little more than a form filed through Ogden, Utah, the same empty co-promote trick Fedor's M-1 tried with the UFC. Floyd already controls half the fight just by making the walk. The problem is the spread: Conor did not get paid what he claims, Floyd knows the made-up number, and he cannot cover it. So why would anyone else step in and take the same loss Floyd will not take himself? Subscribe for more from Chael Sonnen and tell us in the comments: does Floyd vs. Conor 2 ever actually happen? articles.title: Bo Nickal Called It
articles.description: Bo Nickal warned Gable Steveson to his face, and a few weeks later Gable got knocked out. Chael Sonnen was backstage when the warning happened, and he says Bo's whole point now is simple: I told you so. Chael breaks down a feud he admits he found out about late. Bo Nickal and Gable Steveson, both wrestlers, had gone at each other in the media, and Bo confronted Gable backstage at a Real American Freestyle event. Bo's stance was that wrestlers should prop each other up instead of tearing each other down. But his fight take was blunt: Gable is the bigger wrestler and likely beats him in a wrestling match, yet in a fight Gable does not have the reactions or the defenses for strikes yet, and Bo would be able to hit him standing. Then Gable got caught and knocked out, which Chael says proves Bo's premise. From there Chael turns it into a bigger question: is Gable Steveson a heel, does he want to be one, and could it work if he is not willing to live with the boos? A real heel, Chael says, loves the boos, the thumbs down and the middle fingers, because that is the public telling him he is doing his job. Having no opinion about you at all is the road to poverty in this business. And there is a third option that only happens by accident, the cool heel: Chael tells the Stone Cold Steve Austin story, and the Jon Jones press conference moment opposite Daniel Cormier, when Jones said the line he never wanted to say out loud, braced for the crowd to turn on him, and they went crazy for him instead. So what happens if Gable goes heel: do they support him, reject him, or make him extremely monetizable as a cool heel?
